extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of classical (Newtonian) mechanics; readers of advanced mechanics textbooks
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and critical analysis of core Newtonian mechanics concepts (tides, mass, reaction, absolute/relative time/space/motion) intended to define terms, give operational criteria, and illustrate via thought and real experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tidal mechanism via differential lunar acceleration
rubrics_metrics.description: The relative acceleration of the bodies concerned is the tides; the connection of the phenomenon of the tides with the motion of the moon is shown by coincidence of tidal and lunar periods, augmentation at full and new moons, daily retardation (~50 minutes), etc. Free points on the sides nearest to and remotest from the moon acquire different accelerations while the rigid earth as a whole receives one determinate acceleration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table of accelerations for three points A, B, C (free points vs rigid earth) shows that the weight of the water at A and C is diminished by exactly the same amount, so water rises at A and C producing tidal bulges twice every day. Illustrative figures (Fig. 137) and numerical sign-conventions are used. Historical anecdote and observational correlates (periods, phase) support the connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of mutual accelerated motion vs fixed configuration on tide distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: If the moon and the earth were relatively fixed and at rest (no mutual accelerated motion), the phenomenon would be essentially different: the rigid earth acceleration cp would be replaced by zero and the free-point accelerations change accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that hypothetical case the weight at the near side A would be diminished and at the far side C increased, so water elevation would occur only on the side facing the moon (Fig. 138). This contrast clarifies role of mutual acceleration in producing symmetric bulges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tide as an oscillatory movement maintained by the moon
rubrics_metrics.description: The tide should be conceived as an oscillatory movement maintained by the moon rather than a single impulsive displacement produced all at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogy: a fan swept uniformly over a circular canal produces a sustained wave in its wake; likewise the continuous periodic disturbance by the moon maintains tides. Real oceanic tides are further complicated by continents, irregular basins, and periodical variations (reference to Appendix XVII).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of mass by mutual accelerations (operational definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: All those bodies are bodies of equal mass which, mutually acting on each other, produce in each other equal and opposite accelerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines mass by an observable relation (reaction accelerations) rather than by an unclear 'quantity of matter'. It is a naming of a factual relation; 'quantity of matter' is unnecessary. See Appendix XVIII for comparison. Avoid relying on hypothetical atom-counting or chemical homogeneity to define mass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass ratio equals negative inverse ratio of counter-accelerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When two bodies A and B act on each other and acquire accelerations of opposite sign, the ratio of their masses is the negative inverse ratio of those counter-accelerations (B has φ/φ' times the mass of A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If A is taken as unit, assign to it mass m; B's mass is determined by the accelerations imparted in their mutual interaction. This is an operational way to obtain numerical mass-values from dynamics (see Fig. 140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitivity and consistency of mass measurement must be established experimentally
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no logical necessity that two bodies equal to a third (by mutual-action criterion) are equal to each other; consistency (transitivity) of mass values is an empirical fact that must be verified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thought experiments (ring with three elastic bodies A, B, C movable on a frictionless ring — Fig. 141) show contradictions would arise if transitivity failed (e.g., permanent increase of vis viva). Therefore experiments confirm that masses equal to a third are equal to each other, and the order of combination does not influence mass-values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of reaction is redundant given the mass definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The concept of mass, as defined by mutual accelerations, renders unnecessary the separate enunciation of the principle of reaction because the same fact is twice formulated otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two masses i and 2 act on each other, the definition of mass already asserts they impart contrary accelerations to each other in the inverse ratio of their masses; thus Newton's third law is contained within the mass-concept as defined here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass can be measured by weight under constant gravity
rubrics_metrics.description: Mass can be measured by weight where the acceleration of gravity is invariable: if two bodies m and m' are affected oppositely with accelerations φ and φ' and joined so equilibrium holds, then mφ = m'φ'; when φ = φ' (as under gravity) equilibrium implies m = m'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical measurements (string, pulley, two pans of a balance) show mass is replaceable by commensurable weights; the ability to counterbalance pressure by weights provides an exact measure of pressure and thus mass when g is constant. This deduces the common method of weighing from the operational definition of mass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of 'quantity of matter' wording
rubrics_metrics.description: The expression 'quantity of matter' is not adapted to explain the concept of mass because it lacks the requisite clearness and leads to indefensible conceptions, especially when chemical heterogeneity is considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining bodies of equal, chemically homogeneous parts allows a clear idea of quantity; but with heterogeneity, assuming a single measurable 'quantity of matter' is unjustified. Mechanical experimentation supports using the dynamical (accelerational) definition instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute vs relative time (Newtonian distinction and critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newton: 'Absolute, true, and mathematical time, of itself, and by its own nature, flows uniformly on, without regard to anything external.' Relative (apparent) time is a sensible measure of absolute time by motions (hours, days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The textbook criticises absolute time as metaphysical and unmeasurable: time is an abstraction derived from interdependence of changing things; motions are uniform only relative to chosen reference motions. Psychological, historical, and linguistic considerations support construing time from interconnections of events rather than as an independent entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute vs relative space and motion; operational criterion via centrifugal effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Newton: 'Absolute space, in its own nature and without regard to anything external, always remains similar and immovable.' Relative space is a movable measure determined by position relative to other bodies. Absolute motion is translation between absolute places; relative motion is between relative places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects by which absolute and relative motions are distinguished are centrifugal forces in circular motion. Bucket/bucket+water experiment: concave water surface and tendency to recede from axis indicate real (absolute) rotation. Although absolute space's parts are not directly observable, experiments (rotation-induced centrifugal phenomena) give marks to distinguish true from apparent motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical marks exist to guide distinguishing true from apparent motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Although parts of immovable absolute space are not perceptible to our senses, there exist certain marks, abstracted partly from the apparent motions, which guide us to distinguish absolute from relative motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit experimental examples given (bucket experiment, behavior of water and cord-twisting, onset of concavity as relative motion decreases and true rotation increases) illustrate these marks. The textbook emphasizes difficulty but practical viability of identification via inertial/centrifugal effects.
